page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor using the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is delivered through 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 96.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI.

The server contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for system and data persistence. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while no hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs are present. Across standard synthetic benchmarks, the instance delivers mid-tier results for its core count, recording a PassMark CPU score of 28,981.96 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,454.0. In memory throughput tests, the system achieved 128.31 GB/sec in 256 MB uncached reads and 63.76 GB/sec in uncached writes. Small model LLM text generation reached 282.28 tokens per second, though medium model processing dropped to 15.15 tokens per second.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-memory profile and lack of local NVMe storage, the ecs.g7.6xlarge offers predictable resource balance for non-IOPS-intensive production workloads. It is appropriately sized for application servers, static web delivery, distributed caching, and microservices platforms where compute and memory needs scale in equal proportion.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.6xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 96.0 GB of system memory, and a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. It features AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions but includes no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network storage for disk operations. Synthetic benchmarks place the instance in the middle tier for its core class, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 28,981.96 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,454.0, while generating 23.41 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.g7.6xlarge suits standard enterprise application hosting, middle-tier services, and caching workloads.
